rawCommits.subject: fix(observability): clean up status probe agents (#69)
feat(analytics): capture first-touch acquisition source
rawCommits.body:
Classify each visitor's first-touch referrer + utm_source into a clean
acquisition_source label (x, google, direct, or the site's own domain for
anything else) and stamp it once via register_once, so it survives return
visits and rides on every client event. Mirror it onto the user profile
with people.set_once at identify time so server-emitted events like
session_active (True DAU) can also be broken down by source. Lets us see
where signups and engaged/retained users actually come from instead of
guessing. Adds classifier + pipeline tests.

rawCommits.subject: fix(analytics): report a single app_version for the web surface
rawCommits.body:
The Render web build stamps APP_VERSION=$RENDER_GIT_COMMIT, so every deploy
baked a fresh commit SHA into app_version and Mixpanel showed a new web
version per deploy. Web is a single continuously-deployed surface, so
getAppVersion() now reports the unversioned 0.0.0 label for the web platform
(one line in analytics) while desktop and mobile keep their real baked
release versions. The exact web build stays recoverable via
getBuildInfo().commit (bug reports). Affects only the analytics app_version
super-property and the X-App-Version header; no build or validator change.

rendered.title: Cleaner remote agent teardown and sharper acquisition analytics
rendered.intro: Today's nightly tightens two very different seams. On the server, deleting a swarm-hosted agent now actually finishes the job end-to-end, with a graceful stop-then-delete handshake against the swarm gateway. On the web interface, analytics gets meaningfully more trustworthy: every visitor now carries a stable first-touch acquisition source, and the web surface stops inventing a brand-new app_version on every Render deploy.

entries.title: Reliable deletion of swarm-hosted agents
entries.summary: The agent delete handler now understands swarm-mode machines and drives the swarm gateway through a proper stop-then-delete handshake instead of leaving orphaned remote agents behind.

items.text: Agent deletion now detects swarm-mode machines via HarnessMode and routes through the configured SWARM_BASE_URL, returning a clear service-unavailable error when the swarm gateway isn't configured rather than silently dropping the remote agent.

When the gateway reports a 409 that requires stopping first, the server now issues a stop and retries the delete up to twelve times with a 5s backoff, surfacing a bad-gateway error only if the remote agent never finishes stopping.
Backed by new integration coverage for remote delete behavior and refreshed status-probe tooling under infra/evals/status, raising confidence that observability probes exercise the new teardown path.

entries.title: Trustworthy acquisition source and stable web app_version
entries.summary: Two analytics fixes on the web interface: visitors are now tagged with a clean first-touch acquisition source that survives return visits, and the web platform reports one stable app_version instead of a new commit SHA per Render deploy.

items.text: Each visitor's referrer and utm_source are classified into a tidy acquisition_source label (x, google, youtube, reddit, github, linkedin, facebook, hackernews, direct, or the raw domain) and stamped once via register_once so it rides on every client event and survives return visits.
At identify time the source is mirrored onto the user profile with people.set_once, so server-emitted events like session_active (True DAU) can also be broken down by where users actually came from.

getAppVersion() now collapses the continuously-deployed web surface to a single 0.0.0 label so Mixpanel's app_version and the X-App-Version header stop fragmenting on every Render deploy; Desktop and Mobile keep their real baked release versions, and the exact web build remains recoverable via getBuildInfo().commit.

highlights: Remote swarm agents now delete cleanly via stop-then-delete
First-touch acquisition source captured per visitor and mirrored to profiles
Web app_version collapsed to a single label so Mixpanel stops fragmenting per deploy
